newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria sells tool maker for 11.5 mln marks.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria sells tool maker for 11.5 mln marks.

text.p: Bulgaria's Privatisation Agency said on Thursday it has sold 55 percent of Eltos electric tool maker to Sparky Trading GmbH for 11.5 million German marks, payable half in cash and half in government bonds.

Under the deal Berlin-registered Sparky Trading GmbH has to pay five percent of the price in cash in two tranches -- the first on the day of the signing of the contract and the second up to five days later, the agency said in a statement.
The remaining 95 percent of the price are to be paid half in cash and half in long term government bonds up to 45 days after the contract goes into force.
Sparky Trading also pledged to settle 2.252 billion levs of outstanding debts of Lovech-based Eltos and to invest in it 12 million marks over five years.
Eltos produces electric hand drills and jig saws, metal and wood disc cutters and abrasive machines for household and professional use.
Its 1995 turnover amounted to 2.15 billion levs with 85 percent of output exported, the agency said.
Sparky Trading produces and trades in electric tools and has a wide sales network in the former Soviet Union and in Europe, said the agency.

Twenty five percent of the remaining capital of Eltos will be offered for voucher privatisation under Bulgaria's mass sell-off programme and another 20 percent will be offered at preferential prices to Eltos employees.
Multilateral lenders have urged Bulgaria to speed up privatisation which so far has been slow as revenue from sell-offs is seen as a major cash source for this debt-ridden state.
Revenues from privatisation deals, signed by the agency by August 31, totalled 16.3 billion levs.
Bulgaria's privatisation programme for this year projects revenues of around 20 billion levs. -- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 876 032; 981 8569
